name: Lepidium
look_here_first: Examine MATURE SILICLES at 10–20×. L. austrinum often has sparse hairs on the fruit valves and an elliptic-obovate outline; L. virginicum has glabrous, nearly round fruit valves. Confirm with measured fruit width and flower petals.
shared_traits: Annual or biennial mustard herbs with tiny flowers, usually two stamens, elongate fruiting racemes and flattened notched two-seeded silicles.
Upper stem leaves are narrow; basal foliage may be gone by fruiting.

comparison_matrix.austrinum: Sparsely puberulent, sometimes hairs mostly along margin
comparison_matrix.virginicum: Glabrous (very rarely slight pubescence in some treatments)
Orbicular, ~2.5–3.5(–4) mm diameter, widest near middle

decision_sequence: Confirm Lepidium by small, flattened, apically notched silicles and a mustard-family fruit septum.
Inspect several ripe fruit valves at 10–20×: sparse marginal/face hairs favor austrinum; smooth glabrous valves favor virginicum.
Measure fruit length AND width: narrower obovate fruits support austrinum; near-round broader fruits support virginicum.
Use petal size only as support; retain Lepidium sp. when fruit hairs are abraded or traits conflict.
overlap_cautions: Fruit and pedicel lengths overlap; no single size threshold is absolute.
Old fruits can lose hairs; examine multiple fruits and compare margins.
Leaf shape and basal rosette persistence are variable and less decisive than ripe fruit.
Neither source-pool species was canonical in the checked manifest; no native-range certification is implied.

lookalikes.separator: Distinctly triangular/heart-shaped silicles, not Lepidium's nearly round or obovate notched disks.
Short mustard fruits may resemble Lepidium, but inspect fruit shape, valve hairs and flower architecture; avoid naming from a single unripe silicle.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched 10–20× mature silicle faces and margins showing hair presence/absence with mm ruler.
Measured fruits showing length, width, notch and widest point.
Matched petal/sepal side macros and stamen count.
Whole fruiting raceme and mature lower/upper leaves.
handoffs: Diagnostic Photo Polish: acquire matched mature-fruit macros; no photos acquired in this lesson.
Approved Taxa Installer: two source-pool taxa are not canonical; do not install in genus lane.
Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review: inspect any glabrous austrinum-like or pubescent virginicum-like plants against regional key.
